_about: Material level and island archetype rules (docs/design/world-design.md §2–3). The island generator applies ring offsets to the island tier; crafting uses the mean-of-materials rule from the systems PRD §8.4.
_resource_render_note: SWITCH2D (owner 2026-10-21: "keep buildings 3D and make resources 2D"): "card" draws every resource prop as a flat, camera-facing card - the owner's painted sprites (data/world/sprites2d.json) where a family's art is cut, else its baked CARD2D card (data/card2d.json), with data/world/sprites2d_map.json for overrides. "model" is the old 3D GLB look (--models on a lab run). Buildings stay 3D either way.

landing.note: harbour + camp; nothing spawns within 25 m of camp

_wild_level: ASSUMPTION: each level a wild animal sits above its species tier adds this fraction to its health, attack and defense (5 levels = +40 %, ProgressionScaling.LEVEL_STAT_RATE). At or below the tier it keeps its listed stats, so the level-1 starter island is unchanged.

fatigue._about: ASSUMPTION: our own starting values, tune in playtests. Level gap = zone level minus character level. Each level over adds gap_up_rate to every non-baseline fatigue gain, each level under removes gap_down_rate, clamped to [gap_min, gap_max]. Climate fatigue = unmet resistance points x climate_per_min. Window is the seconds a source keeps counting in the breakdown panel.

xp._about: XPECON (islands-and-loop plan section 3.3 'XP economy' + 3.4 knobs): a gather pass pays gather_base + round(its own pass seconds), so a slower node or bare hands pays more and a better tool or skill pays less; a build pays build_first the first time that kit kind is ever placed (memory is World.pioneer_buildings, saved) and build_repeat after that; a build of the same kind within build_spam_radius_m of a standing one of its kind placed less than build_spam_seconds ago pays 0. The level curve stays World.xp_for_level.

gathering_downrank: node level above Gathering skill level is reduced to the skill level
crafted_level: floor(mean of consumed material levels), clamped by governing skill level and recipe max_level

crafting._about: Spec 04 'Crafting skill vs crafting ability' and plan 3.3 'Crafting'. success = clamp(1-(shortfall/100)^2, 0, 1), shortfall = max(0, required_ability - crafting_ability) (0 -> 100 %, 50 -> 75 %, 80 -> 36 %, 100 -> 0 %). CRAFTFEEL note: a recipe without required_ability needs only its min_level (the category-level gate), so today's recipes stay at 100 % (the skewer of spec 25 8 is 100 %); a recipe that declares required_ability can fall short and fail. CRAFTFEEL data (review round 1): every recipe with min_level >= 8 declares required_ability = min_level + 40 (35 recipes, the four min_level 55 raid pieces take 95); this is an ASSUMPTION (gate level + a fixed shortfall headroom), not a balance pass, and every value can be retuned in data alone. The lowest shipped success at a recipe's own gate is 0.840 (raid_maul). A failed craft spends the picked instances and yields nothing (spec 25 8 'if crafting fails, materials disappear'). Flawless is a separate roll on a successful craft (spec 04; its 5 % is plan 3.3's value).
crafting._flawless: A flawless craft keeps its level (a preview must equal the result) and gains stat_bonus: durability x1.1, attributes.quality 'flawless', flags.flawless. flawless_level_bonus only applies to a recipe that sets flawless_level: true.

unstable_flag: all materials from unstable islands until cargo-warped

harbour._about: The harbour stands on the coast (HarbourSite). Its 3x6 footprint's landward row 0 is on land, every cell from dock_from_row to the tip is over water (so the base is within dock_from_row metres of the shoreline), and the tip is at least boat_depth_m below the water line. A pose that breaks this is refused: island build snaps to the nearest legal coast, BuildGrid.can_place answers dock_needs_water / needs_shore. The island json 'harbour' is a hint plus the travel arrival point; t_harbour keeps it on the resolved site.
